contribution.position: Holding my reliability opposition, and answering product's claim that 'nobody else sees a problem' on reliability: that is not a finding, it is an absence of looking. No role in this round has cited any artifact that rebuts artifact:incident-log, which records a 2.4% 30-day error rate against a 0.5% SLO plus two sev2 incidents. Product's cost argument (artifact:cost-sheet, +3% vs 5% ceiling) speaks only to budget, and QA's 412/0 green run (artifact:test-report) measures pre-deploy behavior, not the live SLO breach already in progress. New point this round: with the service already ~5x over its error budget, the change's own blast radius cannot be distinguished from baseline instability during the pilot window, so even a clean deploy would leave us unable to attribute regressions. Reliability remains unsettled until artifact:incident-log is addressed directly or superseded by fresher incident data — none has appeared.
